title: What I changed in Change Stack
intro: I wanted to keep the file, explanation, and review progress connected. I kept file-by-file review and changed how you move between those things.
rows: The layer, file path, and file position are spread across the screen.
I kept the layer, file, and path together. Previous and Next switch files directly; the position opens the searchable nine-file list. Each file keeps its reading position.
Several rows of file controls compete with the diff.
I put frequent file actions in one toolbar and kept Submit review in the PR header. Focus condenses the heading and hides both side panels without losing your place.
The 37-summary count belongs to the layer. access.ts has six.

I labeled both counts and separated summary scope from the selected code. The two access.ts summaries have specific, manually mapped anchors. Other summaries open at their start. The full source summary stays available.
Seen summaries, viewed files, and a submitted review mean different things.
PR progress and the seven included demo files have separate counts. Opening a file never marks it viewed. Summary seen and the final decision stay separate. Viewed changes can be undone.
tradeoff: Split compacts the empty Before panel to 96px and wraps long lines at 13px. Equal panes restores 50/50. The complete function remains readable around an anchor; one highlighted line is not a correctness verdict.
validation: The comparison keeps the same imports, full source summary, and captured progress. I checked anchor jumps, file switching, notes, Undo, keyboard access and Split at 1440px and 1280px. These are implementation checks; developer testing remains outstanding.
scope: This uses the out-of-date Formbricks #8650 snapshot at 23cdac2. Seven of 52 diffs are included. Other content is labeled as a preview; not every source workflow is implemented. Submitting a review is simulated and sends nothing.
next: I’d test whether developers can explain the behavior behind each anchor, and whether compact Split is comfortable to read. Paired-file inspection and a review-wide private question queue remain sketches.
